title: Nonzero scalar multiplication is the principal-quotient restriction kernel
statement: Let A be a commutative domain, f : X -> Spec(A) a flat morphism [def-weil-flat-morphism], L an invertible O_X-module [def-sc-invertible-module], and pi a nonzero element of A. Let i : X times_Spec(A) Spec(A/(pi)) -> X be the first projection, let eta : L -> i_* i^* L be the chosen tensor-pullback adjunction unit [def-pc-module-pullback], and let mu : L -> L be multiplication by the image of pi under A -> Gamma(X,O_X). Then mu composed with eta is zero, and L with map mu is a kernel of eta: the corresponding kernel fork is limiting. There is no valuation-ring, properness, finite-presentation or integral-fibre hypothesis.

source.place: More on Morphisms, Lemma 37.33.3, divisibility step in both proofs; closed-immersion kernel identification from Modules, Tag 08KS.

proof.text: The quotient map A -> A/(pi) is surjective. Its Spec map is a closed immersion and so is its base change i. On an affine chart Spec B of X, tensoring with A/(pi) gives B/pi B; hence the ideal of i is pi O_X. This is the quotient/base-change calculation of Mathlib CommRingCat.isPushout_quotient.

For every open U of X apply injective_smul_sections_of_flat to f restricted to U and to the restriction of L. An open immersion is flat, its composite with f is flat, and restriction preserves invertibility. The scalar is the restriction of the global scalar by appTop naturality. Thus multiplication by pi on every open's sections is injective, giving a monomorphism mu of sheaves.

Apply closedImmersion_unit_kernel to i and L. It identifies the kernel with the image of J tensor L -> L for J = i.ker. The first step identifies J with pi O_X. On each neighbourhood trivializing L, both that image and the image of mu consist exactly of the multiples pi l. Thus the two image subobjects coincide. Since mu is mono by step 2, its source L is isomorphic to the image kernel, and transport of the kernel fork along this isomorphism gives the limiting fork with map mu.

The preceding kernel theorem chooses an adjunction using nonempty_tensorPullbackAdjunction. Compare it with the adjunction chosen from exists_tensorPullbackAdjunction using Adjunction.leftAdjointUniq and Adjunction.unit_leftAdjointUniq_hom_app. The two units differ by an isomorphism of their targets. A kernel fork remains limiting after this invertible change of target, giving exactly the unit and multiplication map of the statement.

proof_origin.place: Fixed nonzero principal-quotient kernel in the divisibility argument, using the existing torsion-free-section and closed-immersion kernel lemmas.

lean.statement:
theorem principal_quotient_unit_kernel
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsDomain A]
    {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of A)) [Flat f]
    (L : X.Modules) [L.IsInvertible] (π : A) (hπ : π ≠ 0) :
    let i := pullback.fst f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom
      (Ideal.Quotient.mk (Ideal.span {π}))))
    let η := (Classical.choose (exists_tensorPullbackAdjunction i)).unit.app L
    let μ := L.smulHom (((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (CommRingCat.of A)).inv ≫ f.appTop).hom π)
    ∃ w : μ ≫ η = 0, Nonempty (IsLimit (KernelFork.ofι μ w))
